rationale: Recorded the peer premise that explains why an emptied node can be driven by a leader it should not recognise: the AppendEntries handler validates only the term and then adopts the sender as leader, with no membership test against r.configurations. That is exactly what receipt 1fb8595fb8664713a0dff87236bde04a index 5 shows when the emptied node follows an outside leader and appends its entry (log 13 to 14) while its own committed log still names {A,B,C}, and receipt 6421d22975164b049baf3e8fc18529d2 index 4 shows the same path refilling the configuration once a legitimate configuration entry arrives. The new source range (raft.go 1473-1492) covers the term check and the leader save, and no execution is claimed beyond the receipts already interpreted.

knowledge.statement: The AppendEntries handler never checks the sender against the configuration: after rejecting only terms older than its own it steps down if needed, adopts the request's address and ID as its leader, and proceeds to the log checks, so a follower accepts entries from any sender whose term is current regardless of whether that sender appears in the receiver's configuration or in the configuration recorded in its log.
knowledge.conditions: An AppendEntries request whose term is not older than the receiver's current term; the receiver holds no configuration entry naming the sender, as when its live configuration is empty or stale relative to its own committed log; the receiver is a follower or steps down on the request.
